pins.emptyHint: Pin a package from the Installed table to keep bulk updates away from it.
pins.suggestIntro: These are depended on by a lot of what you have installed, so a bulk update is more likely to disturb something. Pinning keeps them out of Select all — you can still update them one at a time.
pins.suggestMore_one: {{count}} more package would qualify. Pin some of these, or raise the count in Settings.
pins.suggestMore_other: {{count}} more packages would qualify. Pin some of these, or raise the count in Settings.

requirements.title: Requirements file
requirements.intro: Write this environment out as a requirements.txt, or read one in. Importing previews and snapshots like any other install — it never writes to the environment on its own.

skip.include: names another file, which PipDock has not read
skip.not-from-index: installs from somewhere other than the package index
skip.option: an option that would change how everything installs
skip.unparsed: not a requirement PipDock can read

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.emptyHint: One is taken automatically before every change, and you can take one now.
snapshots.envUnusable: This interpreter cannot be read, so snapshots can be listed but not compared or restored.
snapshots.noDifference: This environment already matches the snapshot.
snapshots.diffAdded_one: {{count}} package here but not in the snapshot — restoring removes it
snapshots.diffAdded_other: {{count}} packages here but not in the snapshot — restoring removes them
snapshots.diffRemoved_one: {{count}} package in the snapshot but not installed — restoring adds it
snapshots.diffRemoved_other: {{count}} packages in the snapshot but not installed — restoring adds them
snapshots.alreadyMatches: Nothing to do — this environment already matches the snapshot.
snapshots.unrestorableDetail: These were installed from a path or a URL rather than from an index, so PipDock cannot fetch them again. Everything else still restores.

cache.title: Disk usage
cache.intro: Everything PipDock has written lives under one folder. Clearing any of these loses only what the line says; nothing about your Python environments changes.
cache.databaseWhy: Not clearable — this one file also holds your settings, your pins and your record of accepting the legal documents. Use Search → Download the index to refresh the package list.

confirm.snapshots: Every snapshot of every environment is removed, and rollback loses its history. Your installed packages are untouched — this deletes the record, not the environment.
confirm.tools: The isolated environment deptry, vulture and ruff run from is removed. The next Code Health run rebuilds it, which needs a network connection.

health.vultureHint: Confidence below 100% can be a false positive — review before deleting.

health.fixBody_other: ruff will apply its safe fixes to {{count}} files.

settings.title: Settings
settings.engineDetail: Which resolver PipDock drives. Both are supported; uv is faster, pip is always present.
settings.pinThresholdDetail: How many other packages must depend on something before the Pins screen suggests pinning it. Zero turns the suggestions off.
settings.overrideDetail: PEP 668 marks some Pythons as managed by the operating system. Installing into one can break system tools, and there is no undo beyond a snapshot. Leave this off unless you know why you need it.

legal.title: Before you start
legal.intro: PipDock changes what is installed in your Python environments. Please read these before continuing:
legal.summary: PipDock is provided without warranty. It runs pip or uv against environments you choose, and every change is previewed and snapshotted first — but you remain responsible for what you install.
legal.accept: I have read and accept these documents.
legal.openFailed: Could not open the link. The documents are on GitHub under poli0981/pipdock.

about.title: About
about.what: PipDock manages what is installed in your Python environments. It drives pip or uv rather than replacing them: every change is previewed before it runs, an environment is snapshotted before it is touched, and a batch reports back package by package when it finishes.
about.privacy: PipDock collects nothing — no telemetry, no account, no self-update. It connects only to PyPI, and the bug-report button opens a prefilled form that you read and send yourself.
about.docsHashDetail: Your acceptance is recorded against this value. Editing any of the documents changes it, and the acceptance screen appears once more on the next launch.
about.aiBody: PipDock was written with substantial help from an AI coding assistant — Claude Opus 5, made by Anthropic — under human review. It wrote source code, tests and translations; every change was read and merged by the maintainer, and the built application was driven by hand before release. Copyright and the GPL-3.0-only licence are unchanged.
about.reopenDetail: Puts the first-run screen back so you can read the five documents. It changes nothing: your acceptance stays as it is, and closing that screen returns you here.
about.contactIntro: PipDock is made by one person. Both addresses are read.
about.contactCode: Source code, security reports and licensing
about.linksIntro: Every other way to get in touch is listed on one page.
